observations: Large stacks of blue plastic barrels/drums, lying on their sides, in an outdoor dirt yard.
Each drum has two small bung-style openings on the end cap, consistent with closed-head industrial drums rather than open-top drums with lift-off lids.
Small white labels with a diamond/hazard-style icon are visible on several drums (photo 0 and photo 1), though text is too small/blurry to read.
Rust-brown staining is visible around some drums, especially near the metal reinforcing rings and bung openings.
No single drum is isolated for close inspection; all shots are of the stacked pile from a middle distance.
Watermark 'EMMALINK CONCEPT NIG' overlays both photos, suggesting a reseller/yard stock photo rather than a photo of the specific unit(s) being sold.
Seller's new message is text only, no new photo or video provided to support the re-assertion.

claims.claim: Food grade, used only once for clean water
claims.evidence: No readable label or certificate visible in photo 0 or photo 1; verbal reassurance in the new message adds no visual proof.
Drums are shown only in a stacked pile at distance in photo 0 and photo 1; no close-up of any single drum's body or base; seller's verbal claim of testing it himself cannot be checked remotely.
Photo 0 and photo 1 show closed-head drums with small round bung openings; no close-up confirms bung caps are present and sealed; no new photo sent.

claims.claim: "I tested it myself yesterday, everything I said is true"
claims.evidence: A personal verbal assurance with no supporting photo, video, or document; cannot be confirmed from a remote text claim alone.

risks.risk: Drums may have previously held chemicals rather than only water, despite the food-grade claim, based on the hazard-style diamond stickers seen in photo 0 and photo 1.
risks.proof: Close-up photo of the label text/UN code on one drum, and a photo of the interior showing no residue or odor description.

risks.risk: Structural damage (cracks, dents, thinning) hidden by the way drums are stacked and photographed only from a distance.
risks.proof: Individual close-up photos or a walk-around video of a few representative drums, including the base.
risks.if_unproven: priced as condition-unverified, i.e. as if some units are damaged

risks.risk: Bung caps missing, stripped, or not sealing properly, which affects usability for liquid storage.
risks.proof: Close-up photo of the bung caps on top of several drums, showing they are present and threaded correctly.

risks.risk: Rust staining near the metal reinforcing rings could indicate these are metal-ringed drums with a rusting band, or could be surface dirt only.
risks.proof: Close-up photo of the rim/ring area on a few drums.
risks.if_unproven: priced as having a rusted/worn ring

risks.risk: Unclear how many drums are included in the sale price (single unit vs. the whole stack/lot).
risks.proof: Seller statement or caption specifying unit count and whether price is per drum or per lot.
risks.if_unproven: priced as per single drum, worst case condition

proof_requests: Close-up, readable photo of the warning/hazard label on at least one drum
Close-up or short video of 2-3 individual drums showing their full body, base, and bung caps, ideally while filling with water to show no leaks
Confirmation of how many drums are covered by the listed price (per unit or per lot)
response.reason: The seller's verbal reassurance adds no new visual evidence, so all claims remain unverified or unverifiable_remote; the drum is still identifiable by type and must be priced at worst case condition until photographic proof is given.
